{"id":"3f5d67cd0a05805b8023c53570998144","title":"Hackathon Page","text":"Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3f5d67cd0a05805b8023c53570998144 as of 2026-10-10T13:13:01.120Z: {"title":"Hackathon Page"} null Ideas; Recruitment agent, use voice chat to build profile, build something that actually matches you to jobs, filter out shit, personal recommendation about how you are feeling, what to do, plans, organise something voice chat, takes in info, asks lots of questions to get information on your profile, finds out what is important to you and builds on that, creates dashbaord for you track habits, plans, jobs, etc --- # AI Conversation Coach — Four-Hour Hackathon Build Plan **Date:** 10 October 2026 **Concept:** An AI role-play simulator for conversations people find difficult. The user speaks out loud to a cartoon/metaverse-style character that answers naturally, challenges them, and gives specific feedback at the end. ## Product pitch **Practice the conversations that matter — before having them for real.** Examples: - Job interview with a realistic hiring manager - Asking a boss for a raise - Breaking up / navigating a difficult relationship conversation - Giving or receiving difficult workplace feedback - Negotiating, setting boundaries, apologising, or handling conflict - Custom user-provided scenario The differentiator is **interactive rehearsal and useful feedback**, not photorealistic avatar technology. ## Scope: what we actually ship in four hours **Must have** - [ ] Choose a scenario and difficulty (friendly / neutral / challenging) - [ ] Display one premade cartoon avatar - [ ] User speaks with live chat - [ ] Gradium transcribes the user's speech - [ ] Gemini generates a brief in-character response using conversation history - [ ] Gradium turns the response into speech - [ ] Avatar switches among idle, listening and speaking animations - [ ] End Session generates a short feedback report **Cut immediately** - [ ] Custom avatar creation from a photo - [ ] Photorealistic lip-sync, body tracking or elaborate gestures - [ ] Authentication, payment, database or saved accounts - [ ] Full-duplex voice interruptions and overlapping speech - [ ] Complex environments, multi-character scenes, multiplayer - [ ] Sophisticated analytics and long transcripts dashboard Photo-to-avatar is not required for this MVP. A premade stylized character plus basic lip movement is sufficient for the demo. ## Proposed technology stack
Layer Technology Responsibility
UI Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind Scenario picker, voice screen, results
Conversation brain Gemini Flash via @google/genai Role-play, follow-up questions, feedback
Voice recognition Gradium STT Convert user's mic audio to text
Voice generation Gradium TTS Read Gemini's answer in character
Avatar Animated 2D SVG **or** premade GLB/VRM Show idle/listening/speaking states
API orchestration Next.js route handlers Protect API keys; coordinate services
Media Browser microphone, HTMLAudioElement Capture/play voice audio
**Choice:** For a reliable four-hour build, prefer a polished animated 2D portrait. Use a premade 3D GLB/VRM only if it already loads and animates. Building an avatar engine is not the product. **Avoid Gemini Live for this particular prototype:** If Gradium must supply both STT and TTS, use Gemini for **text conversation**. Gemini Live's own native audio capabilities would duplicate part of the Gradium pipeline. ## End-to-end architecture 1. User selects scenario + difficulty. 2. Browser records one answer using push-to-talk. 3. POST recorded audio to server API route. 4. Backend sends supported audio to Gradium speech-to-text; obtains a transcript. 5. Backend sends transcript and previous conversation turns to Gemini. 6. Gemini replies as the chosen character, usually 1–3 spoken sentences; backend appends that turn to history. 7. Backend sends Gemini's reply to Gradium text-to-speech and receives audio. 8. Frontend plays the audio and switches avatar to **speaking**. 9. Playback ends; avatar returns to **idle/listening**. 10. User can repeat until they press **End Session**. 11. Gemini evaluates the transcript against a rubric and returns 2 strengths, 2 improvements and 1 suggested better response. **Conceptual flow:** User microphone → Gradium STT → Gemini Flash + history → Gradium TTS → spoken audio + animated avatar. ## Quick setup 1. Get a [Gemini API key](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey). 2. Get a [Gradium API key](https://studio.gradium.ai/). 3. Scaffold a Next.js project and install the Google GenAI SDK. 4. Keep keys on the backend. Never expose Gradium/Gemini keys through NEXT_PUBLIC environment variables. ```bash npx create-next-app@latest conversation-coach cd conversation-coach npm install @google/genai ``` Create .env.local: ```bash GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key GRADIUM_API_KEY=your_key ``` Suggested routes: - POST /api/transcribe — receive user audio; Gradium STT; return text - POST /api/converse — scenario + difficulty + conversation history + user message; Gemini; return reply - POST /api/speak — text; Gradium TTS; return playable WAV audio - POST /api/feedback — conversation transcript + scenario; Gemini; return structured feedback ## Gemini implementation example ```typescript import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"; const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY, }); const response = await ai.models.generateContent({ model: "gemini-2.5-flash", contents: "I'd like to discuss a salary increase.", config: { systemInstruction: "You are a skeptical but fair manager. The user is practising asking for a raise. " + "Stay in character. Ask challenging but believable follow-up questions. " + "Respond in 1–3 natural spoken sentences. Do not coach until the session ends.", }, }); console.log(response.text); ``` For real conversations, send a chat session/history containing **all prior turns**, not only the latest utterance. Keep the role-play consistent with scenario, role and difficulty. Keep replies short to lower latency. ## Gradium voice integration API base: [https://api.gradium.ai](https://api.gradium.ai) - **Speech-to-text:** POST /api/post/speech/asr - **Text-to-speech:** POST /api/post/speech/tts - Follow current official REST request/response details; validate with one sample before building the whole UI. Example server-side TTS request: ```typescript const response = await fetch( "https://api.gradium.ai/api/post/speech/tts", { method: "POST", headers: { "x-api-key": process.env.GRADIUM_API_KEY!, "Content-Type": "application/json", }, body: JSON.stringify({ text: "Why do you believe you deserve a raise?", voice_id: "YTpq7expH9539ERJ", output_format: "wav", only_audio: true, }), } ); if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Gradium TTS failed"); const audio = await response.arrayBuffer(); ``` Return the WAV from the server to the browser with the correct audio content type. Choose an available voice ID from the Gradium docs/dashboard if the example changes. **Important STT gotcha:** MediaRecorder may output WebM/Opus in the browser. Do **not** label WebM as WAV. Either record/encode PCM WAV or convert correctly server-side. Parse the STT response according to the current Gradium docs (including NDJSON segments if returned), concatenating relevant recognised text. **Latency choice:** push-to-talk instead of continuous full-duplex streaming. Finish one turn, get text, generate response, synthesize and play audio, then resume listening. ## Cartoon avatar implementation **Fastest:** animated SVG / 2D character with subtle bobbing, periodic blink and a two-state mouth. Use CSS or Framer Motion if already installed. **If 3D is essential:** use one licensed premade GLB/VRM avatar + Three.js / React Three Fiber; a compatible VRM can use three-vrm for expressions. Frame the upper torso. Avoid the avatar editor entirely. Ready Player Me's former public offering should not be assumed available. Animation states: - **idle**: breathing/bobbing, occasional blink - **listening**: face forward, slight attentiveness - **speaking**: mouth toggles, small nod/head sway during TTS playback ```typescript audio.onplay = () => setIsSpeaking(true); audio.onended = () => setIsSpeaking(false); audio.onerror = () => setIsSpeaking(false); ``` This is an intentionally approximate speaking animation, not phoneme-accurate lip-sync. If there is no mouth blendshape, use an SVG mouth or simple mesh swap instead. ## Scenarios and persona instructions ### Job interview "You are an experienced interviewer assessing a candidate. Ask one question at a time. Demand specific examples and probe vague claims. Remain professional. Do not reveal a rubric or provide coaching until the session ends." ### Asking for a raise "You are the user's manager. You are skeptical but fair about salary increases. Ask for evidence of performance, impact and market value. Raise natural objections. Keep replies concise and conversational." ### Breakup or emotionally difficult conversation "You are the other party in a difficult but respectful relationship conversation. React in a believable, emotionally nuanced way while avoiding threats, manipulation or abuse. Let the user practise empathy and boundaries." ### Difficult feedback "You are a coworker receiving uncomfortable feedback. Start a little defensive, but become more receptive to clear, respectful and specific communication." ### Difficulty settings - **Friendly:** collaborative, gentle objections, lower pressure - **Neutral:** realistic responses and a few challenges - **Challenging:** probing objections, skepticism, follow-up questions without unnecessary hostility System instruction for every scenario: **Stay in character during practice; ask one question at a time; speak naturally in 1–3 sentences; do not prematurely deliver feedback.** A separate Gemini request should generate the final report. ## Interface / demo flow 1. **Landing:** "Practice difficult conversations with AI" 2. **Scenario cards:** Interview / Salary raise / Relationship / Difficult feedback / Custom 3. **Difficulty:** Friendly / Neutral / Challenging 4. **Conversation:** central cartoon avatar, animated state, push-to-talk mic button, small transcript, End Session 5. **Results:** two strengths, two improvements, recommended alternative phrasing; optionally restart at a harder difficulty Demo storyline: select **Ask for a Raise** → speak a salary request → manager challenges the justification by voice → respond once more → End Session → concise actionable report. ## Four-hour sprint checklist ### 00:00–00:45 — Gemini + skeleton UI - [ ] Scaffold Next.js; create scenario picker - [ ] Add /api/converse and persona prompts - [ ] Verify a typed message gets an in-character Gemini response **Checkpoint:** text role-play works, even without voice. ### 00:45–01:40 — Gradium TTS - [ ] Create /api/speak - [ ] Turn a fixed sentence into playable speech - [ ] Wire Gemini responses to automatic audio playback **Checkpoint:** click a button; character's response is heard. ### 01:40–02:35 — Microphone + STT - [ ] Record short user turn - [ ] Convert to compatible audio encoding - [ ] Create /api/transcribe, parse recognized text - [ ] Chain transcription → Gemini → TTS **Checkpoint:** complete two-way voice interaction works. ### 02:35–03:20 — Avatar animation - [ ] Render one premade 2D or 3D avatar - [ ] Implement idle/listening/speaking states - [ ] Hook speaking state to TTS audio playback **Checkpoint:** avatar visibly responds when AI speaks. ### 03:20–04:00 — Feedback + reliability + demo - [ ] Add the scenario/difficulty presets - [ ] End Session report (2 strengths, 2 improvements, improved phrasing) - [ ] Handle microphone denied, empty audio and failed API requests - [ ] Rehearse a complete 2-minute walkthrough **Checkpoint:** demo works from start to finish. ## What could go wrong / fallback plan - **STT audio incompatibility:** test encoding immediately; if blocked, temporarily allow typed input so the rest of the demo remains usable. - **3D avatar takes too long:** revert to a clean 2D SVG character. Animation quality is secondary. - **TTS latency:** keep Gemini replies short, use a loading/speaking state, and avoid huge transcripts per request. - **API quota or model problems:** test keys at the start, show recoverable errors, and have a prerecorded walkthrough/video only as backup for the presentation. - **Unsafe/awkward role-play:** give scenarios clear guardrails; keep relationship simulations respectful and clearly fictional. - **Privacy:** avoid storing raw recordings in MVP unless necessary; get consent if recording or keeping a transcript. ## Definition of done - [ ] A user can select **Ask for a Raise** - [ ] Their spoken words are recognized by Gradium - [ ] Gemini responds in character based on conversation history - [ ] Gradium delivers the response in a spoken voice - [ ] A cartoon avatar animates when speaking - [ ] User can complete at least three turns - [ ] End Session produces clear, useful feedback - [ ] One complete demo can run without editing source code or manually calling APIs ## Copy-paste prompt for Cursor / coding agent > Build a hackathon MVP called Conversation Coach using Next.js App Router, TypeScript and Tailwind. Users select an interview, salary negotiation, breakup conversation, or difficult feedback scenario. Gemini is the conversation AI, using @google/genai with gemini-2.5-flash and full multi-turn history. Gradium must handle both speech-to-text and text-to-speech using the documented REST endpoints. Implement server-side routes /api/transcribe, /api/converse, /api/speak, and /api/feedback; keep keys in GEMINI_API_KEY and GRADIUM_API_KEY server environment variables. Use browser push-to-talk recording, and ensure WAV compatibility for Gradium STT (do not send WebM marked as WAV). Parse Gradium STT responses correctly. Use Gradium TTS with WAV audio output and play it with an HTMLAudioElement. Build a playful, clean cartoon avatar UI with idle/listening/speaking states and simple mouth motion during playback. Prioritize a functional voice loop over complex 3D. Include friendly, neutral and challenging difficulty settings; keep Gemini in character with short spoken replies. Maintain conversation history. Add End Session feedback with 2 strengths, 2 improvements and a suggested better response from Gemini. Add loading, microphone and API error states. No database, authentication, payments, photo-to-avatar generation or unnecessary dependencies. Implement incrementally: text conversation first, then TTS, then STT, then avatar, then feedback. ## Documentation / links - [Gemini API keys](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) - [Google GenAI / Gemini API](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content) - [Gradium Studio](https://studio.gradium.ai/) - [Gradium speech-to-text REST guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/speech-to-text-rest) - [Gradium text-to-speech REST guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/text-to-speech-rest) - [three-vrm for optional 3D avatar](https://github.com/pixiv/three-vrm) **Execution rule:** Do not spend the first two hours making the avatar pretty. First prove the voice conversation loop. The avatar is a presentation layer, not the core value. Features For Demo ","url":"https://app.notion.com/p/3f5d67cd0a05805b8023c53570998144?pvs=204","metadata":{"type":"page"},"cover":null,"icon":null,"verification":{"state":"unverified"},"page_last_edited_at":"2026-10-10T13:13:01.120Z"}

# Conversation Coach

Practise the conversations that matter before having them for real. Choose a scenario and difficulty, speak to an animated counterpart, and finish with two strengths, two improvements and a better way to phrase your response.

Built from the [Notion hackathon plan](https://app.notion.com/p/3f5d67cd0a05805b8023c53570998144). Scenarios: job interview, salary negotiation, relationship conversation, difficult feedback, and a custom scenario.

## Run locally

Use Node.js 22.21 or newer. Install with `npm ci`, copy `.env.example` to `.env.local`, then set `GEMINI_API_KEY` and `GRADIUM_API_KEY`. Run `npm run dev` and open http://127.0.0.1:3000.

Keys stay on the server. The page reports missing provider configuration; it does not substitute canned responses. Conversational turns default to `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`; feedback defaults to `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`. Set `GEMINI_CONVERSATION_MODEL` and `GEMINI_FEEDBACK_MODEL` to override them independently. A legacy `GEMINI_MODEL` setting remains the fallback for either role when its specific setting is absent. The studio defaults to Automatic tone, with optional Marshall or Lainey voice overrides. `GRADIUM_VOICE_ID` remains the fallback for API calls that omit a voice choice. Google Cloud credits and Gemini API billing may differ: use credentials for the endpoint your event account provides.

## Gradium hackathon setup

The [hackathon guide](https://mesquite-pyrite-bca.notion.site/redeem-coupon) funds the voice integration already wired into this app: continuous microphone → Gradium streaming Speech-to-Text → Gemini reply → Gradium streamed Text-to-Speech → spoken counterpart. The coupon is redeemed in your Gradium account; it is not an application API or a source of conversation facts.

1. Get the event's private redemption link from the organizer and redeem it in [Gradium Studio](https://studio.gradium.ai/), using the same email as your hackathon registration.
2. Confirm the credited balance in [Billing](https://studio.gradium.ai/platform/billing), then create a key in [API Keys](https://studio.gradium.ai/platform/api-keys).
3. Set `GRADIUM_API_KEY` in the project's ignored `.env.local` file and restart `npm run dev`. Keep the coupon and key out of the repository and browser code.
4. With the app running at `http://127.0.0.1:3000`, run `npm run check:gradium`. If Next chooses a different port, set `APP_URL`, for example `APP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3001 npm run check:gradium`. This makes one short, credit-consuming synthesis call and transcribes that generated audio through our real app routes. It sends a fixed test sentence, not your conversations, and prints no credentials.

For a distinctive counterpart, use [Voice Design](https://studio.gradium.ai/voices/design) to create and save a synthetic voice. Add its permanent `voice_id` to the server-approved choices in `src/lib/voices.ts` to expose it in the studio; `GRADIUM_VOICE_ID` sets the fallback for API calls without a selection. Example description: “A calm English-speaking hiring manager, clear diction, measured pace, warm but professional.”

For the submission, identify the features as Gradium WebSocket STT and streamed REST TTS, include the selected voice ID, and explain the flow above. TTS currently omits `model_name`, so Gradium chooses its production default; see the [TTS guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/text-to-speech-rest). Coupon redemption, available balance and actual provider access must be checked in your account. The voice check confirms the API path; also try a microphone turn to check recording and playback.

## Demo

The page opens with a short “Got credits? :)” intro, then a sunflower in the rehearsal studio. The Aura visualizer sits behind the sunflower; focus and full-stage controls adjust the layout. Pick an outfit from **The wardrobe** (click a hanger, use the arrows, or ←/→ on the rail), for example **Bazaar negotiation**, and start practising. Give three short answers using the microphone or typed input. End the session to get feedback, then try again using the suggested phrasing.

The microphone uses push-to-talk: click to record, then finish your turn. Audio is encoded as actual mono PCM WAV, not WebM relabelled as WAV. Audio goes to Gradium; the transcript goes to Gemini; Gemini's reply goes to Gradium for spoken output. A typed turn skips transcription. The sunflower’s face mirrors the detected feeling and has listening, thinking and talking states.

## Voice tonality

Each turn, Gemini classifies the tone of the wording of your latest message (`confident`, `calm`, `enthusiastic`, `neutral`, `hesitant`, `nervous`, `defensive`, `frustrated`, `upset`) and picks a tonality for its reply. The page states both in bold, for example “I’m sensing you feel nervous, so I’m adapting a reassuring tone. Hadley is here to train you.” The UI always uses `auto`; the API still accepts a fixed `tonality`, which the server enforces. Tone is judged from words only; Gradium STT returns text, not prosody.

Gradium TTS has no tone parameter: tonality is a property of the voice (its `emotion` tag in Studio). Each tonality maps to a catalog en-US voice in `src/lib/tonality.ts`: calm (Holly), reassuring (Hadley), empathic (Drew), friendly (Wendy), confident (Harrison), excited (Quinn), neutral (Kelsey). Override any of them with `GRADIUM_VOICE_<TONALITY>`, for example `GRADIUM_VOICE_CALM`. The studio defaults to **Automatic tone**. Selecting Marshall or Lainey explicitly overrides the tone-based voice; tone classification and the sunflower’s expression still update. Speech without a tonality or voice selection uses `GRADIUM_VOICE_ID`. Replies stream mono 48 kHz PCM16 into Web Audio as chunks arrive. Reset cancels the request and queued playback; speech errors leave the written reply available.

Conversation turns use minimal thinking on `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` and low thinking on `gemini-3.8-flash`; other model overrides retain their default settings. Gemini 3 thinking tokens count against `maxOutputTokens`; at the default level a short turn could spend its 500-token budget thinking and return truncated JSON.

## Architecture and ownership

| Area | Files | Team responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rehearsal UI | `src/components/`, `src/app/` | Scenarios, avatar, transcript, feedback |
| Microphone | `src/hooks/`, `src/lib/audio.ts`, `src/lib/duplex-session.ts` | Continuous PCM capture, turn detection, WAV fallback and cleanup |
| Conversation | `src/lib/server/`, `src/app/api/converse/` | Gemini prompts and full history |
| Voice services | `src/app/api/transcribe/`, `src/app/api/speak/` | Gradium STT/TTS |
| Reliability | `src/**/*.test.ts`, `e2e/` | Contract, failure and browser checks |

The five-person team can own UI, microphone/voice, conversation/feedback, integration/deployment, and demo/testing separately. All use the shared contracts in `src/lib/contracts.ts`.

## API contracts

| Route | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/status` | None | Provider key presence booleans; never keys |
| `POST /api/voice-token` | None, localhost only | Single-use short-lived `{ token, expires_at }` for browser STT WebSocket |
| `POST /api/transcribe` | Raw `audio/wav` | `{ text, speech }`, where `speech` contains original Gradium segments and any available segment timing |
| `POST /api/converse` | Session and message history | `{ reply, userTone, tonality }` |
| `POST /api/speak` | `{ text, tonality?, voiceId?, format? }` | WAV by default; `format: "pcm"` streams `audio/pcm` with `X-Audio-Sample-Rate: 48000` |
| `POST /api/feedback` | Session and message history | `{ summary, strengths, improvements, suggestedResponse, assessment }`; each assessment dimension contains `{ score, evidence, action }` |

Session input: `scenarioId`, `difficulty`, optional `customScenario`, optional `tonality` (`auto` by default), and `messages` containing `role` (`user` or `assistant`) and `content`. Scenario IDs: `interview`, `raise`, `relationship`, `feedback`, `flatmate`, `coldcall`, `bazaar`, `custom`. Difficulties: `friendly`, `neutral`, `challenging`. Failures return `{ error }` with a non-200 status.

Speech voice IDs are `marshall` and `lainey`, mapped to verified public Gradium catalogue IDs on the server. Speech format accepts `wav` or `pcm`. PCM streaming failures after response headers close the stream; the client retains the transcript and shows a speech error. Reset cancels the request and queued playback.

Completed sessions save their transcript and feedback in a browser-local profile. The app does not save recordings or create accounts. Feedback concerns the words spoken; it does not diagnose personality or mood. Provider retention policies still apply.

Requests are bounded to 64 KiB JSON, 40 messages, 4,000 characters per message and 24,000 characters total. Custom scenarios allow 1,500 characters; speech synthesis accepts 2,000. Recordings allow 60 seconds and 12 MiB, with provider calls limited to 25 seconds. The process-local limit is 60 POST requests per minute across all users; it is a demo safeguard, not a distributed production limiter. Deploying multiple replicas or opening the app publicly needs an appropriate access and usage policy.

## Validation

`npm test` runs unit and API integration tests with mocked providers. `npm run test:coverage` reports service and audio coverage. `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm run build` check the app. Install the test browser with `npx playwright install chromium`, then run `npm run test:e2e` for the browser flow. Mocked tests do not prove real credentials, quotas, microphone hardware or provider latency; validate those with a live three-turn rehearsal.

# AI Conversation Coach — Four-Hour Hackathon Build Plan
**Date:** 10 October 2026  
**Concept:** An AI role-play simulator for conversations people find difficult. The user speaks out loud to a cartoon/metaverse-style character that answers naturally, challenges them, and gives specific feedback at the end.
## Product pitch
**Practice the conversations that matter — before having them for real.**
Examples:
- Job interview with a realistic hiring manager
- Asking a boss for a raise
- Breaking up / navigating a difficult relationship conversation
- Giving or receiving difficult workplace feedback
- Negotiating, setting boundaries, apologising, or handling conflict
- Custom user-provided scenario
The differentiator is **interactive rehearsal and useful feedback**, not photorealistic avatar technology.
## Scope: what we actually ship in four hours
**Must have**
- [ ] Choose a scenario and difficulty (friendly / neutral / challenging)
- [ ] Display one premade cartoon avatar
- [ ] User speaks with live chat
- [ ] Gradium transcribes the user's speech
- [ ] Gemini generates a brief in-character response using conversation history
- [ ] Gradium turns the response into speech
- [ ] Avatar switches among idle, listening and speaking animations
- [ ] End Session generates a short feedback report
**Cut immediately**
- [ ] Custom avatar creation from a photo
- [ ] Photorealistic lip-sync, body tracking or elaborate gestures
- [ ] Authentication, payment, database or saved accounts
- [ ] Full-duplex voice interruptions and overlapping speech
- [ ] Complex environments, multi-character scenes, multiplayer
- [ ] Sophisticated analytics and long transcripts dashboard
Photo-to-avatar is not required for this MVP. A premade stylized character plus basic lip movement is sufficient for the demo.

**Avoid Gemini Live for this particular prototype:** If Gradium must supply both STT and TTS, use Gemini for **text conversation**. Gemini Live's own native audio capabilities would duplicate part of the Gradium pipeline.
## End-to-end architecture
1. User selects scenario + difficulty.
2. Browser records one answer using push-to-talk.
3. POST recorded audio to server API route.
4. Backend sends supported audio to Gradium speech-to-text; obtains a transcript.
5. Backend sends transcript and previous conversation turns to Gemini.
6. Gemini replies as the chosen character, usually 1–3 spoken sentences; backend appends that turn to history.
7. Backend sends Gemini's reply to Gradium text-to-speech and receives audio.
8. Frontend plays the audio and switches avatar to **speaking**.
9. Playback ends; avatar returns to **idle/listening**.
10. User can repeat until they press **End Session**.
11. Gemini evaluates the transcript against a rubric and returns 2 strengths, 2 improvements and 1 suggested better response.
**Conceptual flow:** User microphone → Gradium STT → Gemini Flash + history → Gradium TTS → spoken audio + animated avatar.

1. Get a [Gemini API key](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey).
2. Get a [Gradium API key](https://studio.gradium.ai/).
3. Scaffold a Next.js project and install the Google GenAI SDK.
4. Keep keys on the backend. Never expose Gradium/Gemini keys through NEXT_PUBLIC environment variables.
```bash
npx create-next-app@latest conversation-coach
cd conversation-coach
npm install @google/genai
```
Create .env.local:
```bash
GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key
GRADIUM_API_KEY=your_key
```
Suggested routes:
- POST /api/transcribe — receive user audio; Gradium STT; return text
- POST /api/converse — scenario + difficulty + conversation history + user message; Gemini; return reply
- POST /api/speak — text; Gradium TTS; return playable WAV audio
- POST /api/feedback — conversation transcript + scenario; Gemini; return structured feedback
## Gemini implementation example
```typescript
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";

const ai = new GoogleGenAI({
  apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY,
});

const response = await ai.models.generateContent({
  model: "gemini-2.5-flash",
  contents: "I'd like to discuss a salary increase.",
  config: {
    systemInstruction:
      "You are a skeptical but fair manager. The user is practising asking for a raise. " +
      "Stay in character. Ask challenging but believable follow-up questions. " +
      "Respond in 1–3 natural spoken sentences. Do not coach until the session ends.",
  },
});

console.log(response.text);
```
For real conversations, send a chat session/history containing **all prior turns**, not only the latest utterance. Keep the role-play consistent with scenario, role and difficulty. Keep replies short to lower latency.
## Gradium voice integration
API base: [https://api.gradium.ai](https://api.gradium.ai)
- **Speech-to-text:** POST /api/post/speech/asr
- **Text-to-speech:** POST /api/post/speech/tts
- Follow current official REST request/response details; validate with one sample before building the whole UI.
Example server-side TTS request:
```typescript
const response = await fetch(
  "https://api.gradium.ai/api/post/speech/tts",
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "x-api-key": process.env.GRADIUM_API_KEY!,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      text: "Why do you believe you deserve a raise?",
      voice_id: "YTpq7expH9539ERJ",
      output_format: "wav",
      only_audio: true,
    }),
  }
);

if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Gradium TTS failed");
const audio = await response.arrayBuffer();
```
Return the WAV from the server to the browser with the correct audio content type. Choose an available voice ID from the Gradium docs/dashboard if the example changes.
**Important STT gotcha:** MediaRecorder may output WebM/Opus in the browser. Do **not** label WebM as WAV. Either record/encode PCM WAV or convert correctly server-side. Parse the STT response according to the current Gradium docs (including NDJSON segments if returned), concatenating relevant recognised text.
**Latency choice:** push-to-talk instead of continuous full-duplex streaming. Finish one turn, get text, generate response, synthesize and play audio, then resume listening.
## Cartoon avatar implementation
**Fastest:** animated SVG / 2D character with subtle bobbing, periodic blink and a two-state mouth. Use CSS or Framer Motion if already installed.
**If 3D is essential:** use one licensed premade GLB/VRM avatar + Three.js / React Three Fiber; a compatible VRM can use three-vrm for expressions. Frame the upper torso. Avoid the avatar editor entirely. Ready Player Me's former public offering should not be assumed available.
Animation states:
- **idle**: breathing/bobbing, occasional blink
- **listening**: face forward, slight attentiveness
- **speaking**: mouth toggles, small nod/head sway during TTS playback
```typescript
audio.onplay = () => setIsSpeaking(true);
audio.onended = () => setIsSpeaking(false);
audio.onerror = () => setIsSpeaking(false);
```
This is an intentionally approximate speaking animation, not phoneme-accurate lip-sync. If there is no mouth blendshape, use an SVG mouth or simple mesh swap instead.
## Scenarios and persona instructions
### Job interview
"You are an experienced interviewer assessing a candidate. Ask one question at a time. Demand specific examples and probe vague claims. Remain professional. Do not reveal a rubric or provide coaching until the session ends."
### Asking for a raise
"You are the user's manager. You are skeptical but fair about salary increases. Ask for evidence of performance, impact and market value. Raise natural objections. Keep replies concise and conversational."
### Breakup or emotionally difficult conversation
"You are the other party in a difficult but respectful relationship conversation. React in a believable, emotionally nuanced way while avoiding threats, manipulation or abuse. Let the user practise empathy and boundaries."
### Difficult feedback
"You are a coworker receiving uncomfortable feedback. Start a little defensive, but become more receptive to clear, respectful and specific communication."
### Difficulty settings
- **Friendly:** collaborative, gentle objections, lower pressure
- **Neutral:** realistic responses and a few challenges
- **Challenging:** probing objections, skepticism, follow-up questions without unnecessary hostility
System instruction for every scenario: **Stay in character during practice; ask one question at a time; speak naturally in 1–3 sentences; do not prematurely deliver feedback.** A separate Gemini request should generate the final report.
## Interface / demo flow
1. **Landing:** "Practice difficult conversations with AI"
2. **Scenario cards:** Interview / Salary raise / Relationship / Difficult feedback / Custom
3. **Difficulty:** Friendly / Neutral / Challenging
4. **Conversation:** central cartoon avatar, animated state, push-to-talk mic button, small transcript, End Session
5. **Results:** two strengths, two improvements, recommended alternative phrasing; optionally restart at a harder difficulty
Demo storyline: select **Ask for a Raise** → speak a salary request → manager challenges the justification by voice → respond once more → End Session → concise actionable report.
## Four-hour sprint checklist
### 00:00–00:45 — Gemini + skeleton UI
- [ ] Scaffold Next.js; create scenario picker
- [ ] Add /api/converse and persona prompts
- [ ] Verify a typed message gets an in-character Gemini response
**Checkpoint:** text role-play works, even without voice.
### 00:45–01:40 — Gradium TTS
- [ ] Create /api/speak
- [ ] Turn a fixed sentence into playable speech
- [ ] Wire Gemini responses to automatic audio playback
**Checkpoint:** click a button; character's response is heard.
### 01:40–02:35 — Microphone + STT
- [ ] Record short user turn
- [ ] Convert to compatible audio encoding
- [ ] Create /api/transcribe, parse recognized text
- [ ] Chain transcription → Gemini → TTS
**Checkpoint:** complete two-way voice interaction works.
### 02:35–03:20 — Avatar animation
- [ ] Render one premade 2D or 3D avatar
- [ ] Implement idle/listening/speaking states
- [ ] Hook speaking state to TTS audio playback
**Checkpoint:** avatar visibly responds when AI speaks.
### 03:20–04:00 — Feedback + reliability + demo
- [ ] Add the scenario/difficulty presets
- [ ] End Session report (2 strengths, 2 improvements, improved phrasing)
- [ ] Handle microphone denied, empty audio and failed API requests
- [ ] Rehearse a complete 2-minute walkthrough
**Checkpoint:** demo works from start to finish.

- **STT audio incompatibility:** test encoding immediately; if blocked, temporarily allow typed input so the rest of the demo remains usable.
- **3D avatar takes too long:** revert to a clean 2D SVG character. Animation quality is secondary.
- **TTS latency:** keep Gemini replies short, use a loading/speaking state, and avoid huge transcripts per request.
- **API quota or model problems:** test keys at the start, show recoverable errors, and have a prerecorded walkthrough/video only as backup for the presentation.
- **Unsafe/awkward role-play:** give scenarios clear guardrails; keep relationship simulations respectful and clearly fictional.
- **Privacy:** avoid storing raw recordings in MVP unless necessary; get consent if recording or keeping a transcript.
## Definition of done
- [ ] A user can select **Ask for a Raise**
- [ ] Their spoken words are recognized by Gradium
- [ ] Gemini responds in character based on conversation history
- [ ] Gradium delivers the response in a spoken voice
- [ ] A cartoon avatar animates when speaking
- [ ] User can complete at least three turns
- [ ] End Session produces clear, useful feedback
- [ ] One complete demo can run without editing source code or manually calling APIs

Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3f5d67cd0a05805b8023c53570998144 as of 2026-10-10T13:13:01.120Z: {"title":"Hackathon Page"} null Ideas; Recruitment agent, use voice chat to build profile, build something that actually matches you to jobs, filter out shit, personal recommendation about how you are feeling, what to do, plans, organise something voice chat, takes in info, asks lots of questions to get information on your profile, finds out what is important to you and builds on that, creates dashbaord for you track habits, plans, jobs, etc --- # AI Conversation Coach — Four-Hour Hackathon Build Plan **Date:** 10 October 2026 **Concept:** An AI role-play simulator for conversations people find difficult. The user speaks out loud to a cartoon/metaverse-style character that answers naturally, challenges them, and gives specific feedback at the end. ## Product pitch **Practice the conversations that matter — before having them for real.** Examples: - Job interview with a realistic hiring manager - Asking a boss for a raise - Breaking up / navigating a difficult relationship conversation - Giving or receiving difficult workplace feedback - Negotiating, setting boundaries, apologising, or handling conflict - Custom user-provided scenario The differentiator is **interactive rehearsal and useful feedback**, not photorealistic avatar technology. ## Scope: what we actually ship in four hours **Must have** - [ ] Choose a scenario and difficulty (friendly / neutral / challenging) - [ ] Display one premade cartoon avatar - [ ] User speaks with live chat - [ ] Gradium transcribes the user's speech - [ ] Gemini generates a brief in-character response using conversation history - [ ] Gradium turns the response into speech - [ ] Avatar switches among idle, listening and speaking animations - [ ] End Session generates a short feedback report **Cut immediately** - [ ] Custom avatar creation from a photo - [ ] Photorealistic lip-sync, body tracking or elaborate gestures - [ ] Authentication, payment, database or saved accounts - [ ] Full-duplex voice interruptions and overlapping speech - [ ] Complex environments, multi-character scenes, multiplayer - [ ] Sophisticated analytics and long transcripts dashboard Photo-to-avatar is not required for this MVP. A premade stylized character plus basic lip movement is sufficient for the demo. ## Proposed technology stack
Layer Technology Responsibility
UI Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind Scenario picker, voice screen, results
Conversation brain Gemini Flash via @google/genai Role-play, follow-up questions, feedback
Voice recognition Gradium STT Convert user's mic audio to text
Voice generation Gradium TTS Read Gemini's answer in character
Avatar Animated 2D SVG **or** premade GLB/VRM Show idle/listening/speaking states
API orchestration Next.js route handlers Protect API keys; coordinate services
Media Browser microphone, HTMLAudioElement Capture/play voice audio
**Choice:** For a reliable four-hour build, prefer a polished animated 2D portrait. Use a premade 3D GLB/VRM only if it already loads and animates. Building an avatar engine is not the product. **Avoid Gemini Live for this particular prototype:** If Gradium must supply both STT and TTS, use Gemini for **text conversation**. Gemini Live's own native audio capabilities would duplicate part of the Gradium pipeline. ## End-to-end architecture 1. User selects scenario + difficulty. 2. Browser records one answer using push-to-talk. 3. POST recorded audio to server API route. 4. Backend sends supported audio to Gradium speech-to-text; obtains a transcript. 5. Backend sends transcript and previous conversation turns to Gemini. 6. Gemini replies as the chosen character, usually 1–3 spoken sentences; backend appends that turn to history. 7. Backend sends Gemini's reply to Gradium text-to-speech and receives audio. 8. Frontend plays the audio and switches avatar to **speaking**. 9. Playback ends; avatar returns to **idle/listening**. 10. User can repeat until they press **End Session**. 11. Gemini evaluates the transcript against a rubric and returns 2 strengths, 2 improvements and 1 suggested better response. **Conceptual flow:** User microphone → Gradium STT → Gemini Flash + history → Gradium TTS → spoken audio + animated avatar. ## Quick setup 1. Get a [Gemini API key](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey). 2. Get a [Gradium API key](https://studio.gradium.ai/). 3. Scaffold a Next.js project and install the Google GenAI SDK. 4. Keep keys on the backend. Never expose Gradium/Gemini keys through NEXT_PUBLIC environment variables. ```bash npx create-next-app@latest conversation-coach cd conversation-coach npm install @google/genai ``` Create .env.local: ```bash GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key GRADIUM_API_KEY=your_key ``` Suggested routes: - POST /api/transcribe — receive user audio; Gradium STT; return text - POST /api/converse — scenario + difficulty + conversation history + user message; Gemini; return reply - POST /api/speak — text; Gradium TTS; return playable WAV audio - POST /api/feedback — conversation transcript + scenario; Gemini; return structured feedback ## Gemini implementation example ```typescript import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"; const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY, }); const response = await ai.models.generateContent({ model: "gemini-2.5-flash", contents: "I'd like to discuss a salary increase.", config: { systemInstruction: "You are a skeptical but fair manager. The user is practising asking for a raise. " + "Stay in character. Ask challenging but believable follow-up questions. " + "Respond in 1–3 natural spoken sentences. Do not coach until the session ends.", }, }); console.log(response.text); ``` For real conversations, send a chat session/history containing **all prior turns**, not only the latest utterance. Keep the role-play consistent with scenario, role and difficulty. Keep replies short to lower latency. ## Gradium voice integration API base: [https://api.gradium.ai](https://api.gradium.ai) - **Speech-to-text:** POST /api/post/speech/asr - **Text-to-speech:** POST /api/post/speech/tts - Follow current official REST request/response details; validate with one sample before building the whole UI. Example server-side TTS request: ```typescript const response = await fetch( "https://api.gradium.ai/api/post/speech/tts", { method: "POST", headers: { "x-api-key": process.env.GRADIUM_API_KEY!, "Content-Type": "application/json", }, body: JSON.stringify({ text: "Why do you believe you deserve a raise?", voice_id: "YTpq7expH9539ERJ", output_format: "wav", only_audio: true, }), } ); if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Gradium TTS failed"); const audio = await response.arrayBuffer(); ``` Return the WAV from the server to the browser with the correct audio content type. Choose an available voice ID from the Gradium docs/dashboard if the example changes. **Important STT gotcha:** MediaRecorder may output WebM/Opus in the browser. Do **not** label WebM as WAV. Either record/encode PCM WAV or convert correctly server-side. Parse the STT response according to the current Gradium docs (including NDJSON segments if returned), concatenating relevant recognised text. **Latency choice:** push-to-talk instead of continuous full-duplex streaming. Finish one turn, get text, generate response, synthesize and play audio, then resume listening. ## Cartoon avatar implementation **Fastest:** animated SVG / 2D character with subtle bobbing, periodic blink and a two-state mouth. Use CSS or Framer Motion if already installed. **If 3D is essential:** use one licensed premade GLB/VRM avatar + Three.js / React Three Fiber; a compatible VRM can use three-vrm for expressions. Frame the upper torso. Avoid the avatar editor entirely. Ready Player Me's former public offering should not be assumed available. Animation states: - **idle**: breathing/bobbing, occasional blink - **listening**: face forward, slight attentiveness - **speaking**: mouth toggles, small nod/head sway during TTS playback ```typescript audio.onplay = () => setIsSpeaking(true); audio.onended = () => setIsSpeaking(false); audio.onerror = () => setIsSpeaking(false); ``` This is an intentionally approximate speaking animation, not phoneme-accurate lip-sync. If there is no mouth blendshape, use an SVG mouth or simple mesh swap instead. ## Scenarios and persona instructions ### Job interview "You are an experienced interviewer assessing a candidate. Ask one question at a time. Demand specific examples and probe vague claims. Remain professional. Do not reveal a rubric or provide coaching until the session ends." ### Asking for a raise "You are the user's manager. You are skeptical but fair about salary increases. Ask for evidence of performance, impact and market value. Raise natural objections. Keep replies concise and conversational." ### Breakup or emotionally difficult conversation "You are the other party in a difficult but respectful relationship conversation. React in a believable, emotionally nuanced way while avoiding threats, manipulation or abuse. Let the user practise empathy and boundaries." ### Difficult feedback "You are a coworker receiving uncomfortable feedback. Start a little defensive, but become more receptive to clear, respectful and specific communication." ### Difficulty settings - **Friendly:** collaborative, gentle objections, lower pressure - **Neutral:** realistic responses and a few challenges - **Challenging:** probing objections, skepticism, follow-up questions without unnecessary hostility System instruction for every scenario: **Stay in character during practice; ask one question at a time; speak naturally in 1–3 sentences; do not prematurely deliver feedback.** A separate Gemini request should generate the final report. ## Interface / demo flow 1. **Landing:** "Practice difficult conversations with AI" 2. **Scenario cards:** Interview / Salary raise / Relationship / Difficult feedback / Custom 3. **Difficulty:** Friendly / Neutral / Challenging 4. **Conversation:** central cartoon avatar, animated state, push-to-talk mic button, small transcript, End Session 5. **Results:** two strengths, two improvements, recommended alternative phrasing; optionally restart at a harder difficulty Demo storyline: select **Ask for a Raise** → speak a salary request → manager challenges the justification by voice → respond once more → End Session → concise actionable report. ## Four-hour sprint checklist ### 00:00–00:45 — Gemini + skeleton UI - [ ] Scaffold Next.js; create scenario picker - [ ] Add /api/converse and persona prompts - [ ] Verify a typed message gets an in-character Gemini response **Checkpoint:** text role-play works, even without voice. ### 00:45–01:40 — Gradium TTS - [ ] Create /api/speak - [ ] Turn a fixed sentence into playable speech - [ ] Wire Gemini responses to automatic audio playback **Checkpoint:** click a button; character's response is heard. ### 01:40–02:35 — Microphone + STT - [ ] Record short user turn - [ ] Convert to compatible audio encoding - [ ] Create /api/transcribe, parse recognized text - [ ] Chain transcription → Gemini → TTS **Checkpoint:** complete two-way voice interaction works. ### 02:35–03:20 — Avatar animation - [ ] Render one premade 2D or 3D avatar - [ ] Implement idle/listening/speaking states - [ ] Hook speaking state to TTS audio playback **Checkpoint:** avatar visibly responds when AI speaks. ### 03:20–04:00 — Feedback + reliability + demo - [ ] Add the scenario/difficulty presets - [ ] End Session report (2 strengths, 2 improvements, improved phrasing) - [ ] Handle microphone denied, empty audio and failed API requests - [ ] Rehearse a complete 2-minute walkthrough **Checkpoint:** demo works from start to finish. ## What could go wrong / fallback plan - **STT audio incompatibility:** test encoding immediately; if blocked, temporarily allow typed input so the rest of the demo remains usable. - **3D avatar takes too long:** revert to a clean 2D SVG character. Animation quality is secondary. - **TTS latency:** keep Gemini replies short, use a loading/speaking state, and avoid huge transcripts per request. - **API quota or model problems:** test keys at the start, show recoverable errors, and have a prerecorded walkthrough/video only as backup for the presentation. - **Unsafe/awkward role-play:** give scenarios clear guardrails; keep relationship simulations respectful and clearly fictional. - **Privacy:** avoid storing raw recordings in MVP unless necessary; get consent if recording or keeping a transcript. ## Definition of done - [ ] A user can select **Ask for a Raise** - [ ] Their spoken words are recognized by Gradium - [ ] Gemini responds in character based on conversation history - [ ] Gradium delivers the response in a spoken voice - [ ] A cartoon avatar animates when speaking - [ ] User can complete at least three turns - [ ] End Session produces clear, useful feedback - [ ] One complete demo can run without editing source code or manually calling APIs ## Copy-paste prompt for Cursor / coding agent > Build a hackathon MVP called Conversation Coach using Next.js App Router, TypeScript and Tailwind. Users select an interview, salary negotiation, breakup conversation, or difficult feedback scenario. Gemini is the conversation AI, using @google/genai with gemini-2.5-flash and full multi-turn history. Gradium must handle both speech-to-text and text-to-speech using the documented REST endpoints. Implement server-side routes /api/transcribe, /api/converse, /api/speak, and /api/feedback; keep keys in GEMINI_API_KEY and GRADIUM_API_KEY server environment variables. Use browser push-to-talk recording, and ensure WAV compatibility for Gradium STT (do not send WebM marked as WAV). Parse Gradium STT responses correctly. Use Gradium TTS with WAV audio output and play it with an HTMLAudioElement. Build a playful, clean cartoon avatar UI with idle/listening/speaking states and simple mouth motion during playback. Prioritize a functional voice loop over complex 3D. Include friendly, neutral and challenging difficulty settings; keep Gemini in character with short spoken replies. Maintain conversation history. Add End Session feedback with 2 strengths, 2 improvements and a suggested better response from Gemini. Add loading, microphone and API error states. No database, authentication, payments, photo-to-avatar generation or unnecessary dependencies. Implement incrementally: text conversation first, then TTS, then STT, then avatar, then feedback. ## Documentation / links - [Gemini API keys](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) - [Google GenAI / Gemini API](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content) - [Gradium Studio](https://studio.gradium.ai/) - [Gradium speech-to-text REST guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/speech-to-text-rest) - [Gradium text-to-speech REST guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/text-to-speech-rest) - [three-vrm for optional 3D avatar](https://github.com/pixiv/three-vrm) **Execution rule:** Do not spend the first two hours making the avatar pretty. First prove the voice conversation loop. The avatar is a presentation layer, not the core value. Features For Demo

Data cell Data cell

Do not include a element if you do not want to set any column colors or widths. - : Column definition with optional attributes: - color: The color of the column - width: The width of the column. Leave empty to auto-size. - : Table row with optional color attribute - ) 3. Column color () Contents of table cells: - Table cells can only contain rich text. Other block types (headings, lists, images, etc.) are not supported. - Never use raw HTML formatting tags inside table cells; use the equivalent Notion-flavored Markdown instead, for example **bold** instead of or . Cell merging: - Notion supports merging rectangular groups of cells into a single cell. - You cannot create or modify cell merges through this format. If the user asks you to merge cells, tell them Notion supports it but they must do it in the UI: select the cells, right-click, and choose "Merge cells". Do NOT escape special characters inside code blocks. Code block content is literal - write it exactly as it should appear. For example, write `const arr = [1, 2, 3]` NOT `const arr = \[1, 2, 3\]`. ` for line breaks inside node labels, not \n. Do not use \( or \) inside Mermaid — instead just wrap the whole label in double quotes. XML blocks use the 'color' attribute to set a block color. A user URL has the form user://. The inner text (name/title) is optional. The UI always displays the resolved name. So an alternative self-closing format is also supported: Mentions are clickable and link to the entity. For dates and datetimes, omit the 'end' attribute to mention a single date or datetime. startTime requires timeZone; without timeZone the time is dropped. A datetime range needs all five attributes: start, startTime, end, endTime, and timeZone. is an inline reference only. Do NOT use it to replace a block — removing a block deletes the child page. Toggle:
Rich text Children

If you do not indent the children, they will not be contained within the toggle or toggle heading. Callout: Rich text Children Callouts can contain multiple blocks and nested children, not just inline rich text. Each child block should be indented. For any formatting inside of callout blocks, use Notion-flavored Markdown, not HTML. For instance, bold text in a callout should be wrapped in **, not . Columns: Children Children - ratio: Optional column width as a percentage of the full width, e.g. 50 for half. Omit it to use the default even split when creating columns. When updating existing columns, set every ratio explicitly. Tabs: Tab title Children Each must have its title as the first indented line. The optional icon attribute accepts an emoji or Notion Icon, such as icon="icons/document_gray". Custom emoji: :emoji_name: Page: Title IMPORTANT: A tag represents a subpage (child page) on the current page. WARNING: Using with an existing page URL will MOVE that page into this page as a subpage. Removing that tag from the content will REMOVE that child page from the current page. If moving is not intended use the block instead. Folder: Title A tag represents an existing folder. Use the URL with loadFolder (or fetch in MCP) to read the folder's immediate children, then follow nested URLs to continue traversing. Preserve existing folder tags unless intentionally moving or deleting the folder. Folders cannot be created from Markdown. Database: Title Provide either url or data-source-url attribute: - If 'url' is an existing database URL, including it here will MOVE that database into the current page. If you just want to mention an existing database, use instead. - If 'data-source-url' is an existing data source URL, creates a linked database view. The 'inline' attribute toggles how the database is displayed in the UI. If set to "true", the database is fully visible and interactive on the page. If set to "false", the database is displayed as a sub-page. If you try to set inline to an invalid value, it will default to "false". The 'wiki' attribute indicates whether this database is a wiki. Wiki databases have wiki="true". When creating pages in a wiki database, you MUST use parent type "page" with the wiki's page URL instead of parent type "dataSource". Wiki pages must be created under the database page, not the data source directly. There is no 'Data Source' block type. Data Sources are always inside a Database, and only Databases can be inserted into a Page. Audio: File: Caption Embed (renders an HTML attachment file inline in a sandboxed iframe): Caption "HTML", "HTML block", "HTML artifact", and "HTML embed" all mean an HTML attachment rendered with . Never create one as a code block or file block. Always use for HTML attachment files For files created by the MCP create-attachment tool, use its returned file-upload:// source as the src value. The source is resolved and attached when create-pages or update-page saves the block. Keep the returned file upload ID if you need to retrieve the text later with download-attachment. For files uploaded through the MCP create-file-upload flow, use the upload response's suggested_markdown directly in create-pages or update-page content. To attach the upload to a comment, include suggested_markdown on a separate line in create-comment markdown; comments support up to three file attachments. Image: ![Caption](URL) {color?="Color"} PDF: Caption Video: (Note that source URLs can either be compressed URLs, such as src="{{1}}", or full URLs, such as src="example.com". Full URLs enclosed in curly brackets, like src="{{https://example.com}}" or src="{{example.com}}", do not work.) Table of contents: Synced block: The original source for a synced block. Children Note: When creating new synced blocks, omit the url attribute - it will be auto-generated. When reading existing synced blocks, the url attribute will be present. Synced block reference: A reference to a synced block. The synced block must already exist and url must be provided. You can directly update the children of the synced block reference and it will update both the original synced block and the synced block reference. If content is unavailable due to permissions, a non-editable notice may be included via the optional notice attribute. Children Meeting notes: Rich text (meeting title) AI-generated summary of the notes + transcript User notes Transcript of the audio (cannot be edited) - The tag contains a raw transcript and cannot be edited by AI, but it can be edited by a user. - When creating new meeting notes blocks, you must omit the and tags. - Only include in a new meeting notes block if the user is SPECIFICALLY requesting note content. - Attempting to include or edit will result in an error. - All content within , , and tags must be indented at least one level deeper than the tag. Custom blocks: Omit url when creating a new instance. Readback adds its instance URL; preserve that URL when editing, reordering, or moving an existing instance. Place the self-closing tag on its own line. It references a saved definition in the destination workspace and inherits its bindings; it does not contain rendered content or instance binding overrides. New placements and definition changes require a live definition readable by the caller. Retaining the same existing instance and definition does not require fresh definition access, even if the definition was deleted. Adding another instance still requires authorization. Public API and MCP requests reject definition-key, which is reserved for App deployments. Reading or placing an existing definition through Markdown does not require separate workspace enablement; definition creation remains in private alpha. Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/implementation_audit
Payload:
Read-only audit complete. Code evidence supports checking these as implemented:

- Main app path: `src/app/page.tsx` renders `Coach`, so the demo surface is the coach UI.
- Scenarios: built-in `interview`, `raise`, `relationship`, `feedback`, `flatmate`, `coldcall`, `bazaar`, and `custom` exist in `src/lib/scenarios.ts:1-54`; UI selects them in `Coach` at `src/components/coach.tsx:421-433`.
- Wardrobe/outfit selector: `Wardrobe` maps outfits to scenario IDs and changes the selected scenario in `src/components/wardrobe.tsx:6-27`; `Coach` renders it before session start at `src/components/coach.tsx:425`.
- Avatar/sunflower: `Coach` renders both `Avatar` and `Sunflower` in the stage at `src/components/coach.tsx:490-494`; `Avatar` has idle/listening/thinking/speaking states in `src/components/avatar.tsx:6-91`; `Sunflower` maps moods/outfits to SVG face/outfit states in `src/components/sunflower.tsx:45-84`.
- Text conversation: composer calls `runTurn('text')` and posts to `/api/converse` at `src/components/coach.tsx:627-640`; API validates and calls Gemini in `src/app/api/converse/route.ts:5-11`.
- Manual voice answer: record button starts/stops `useVoiceSession` at `src/components/coach.tsx:542-550`; hook captures microphone audio, live partial transcript, and WAV encoding in `src/hooks/use-voice-session.ts:87-147`; `/api/transcribe` calls Gradium ASR in `src/app/api/transcribe/route.ts:4-10`.
- Live voice: “Start live voice” button calls `startLive` at `src/components/coach.tsx:535-540`; `createDuplexSession` handles continuous mic, Gradium websocket ASR, turn flush, and interruption in `src/lib/duplex-session.ts:40-175`.
- Voice output: assistant replies call `/api/speak` with PCM streaming in `src/components/coach.tsx:180-199`; route supports `pcm` and `wav` in `src/app/api/speak/route.ts:5-18`.
- Feedback/report: `finish()` posts `/api/feedback`, saves the returned report, and opens `SessionReport` at `src/components/coach.tsx:241-259`; feedback route validates with `feedbackInputSchema` in `src/app/api/feedback/route.ts:5-6`; report UI includes scores, progress, answer review, suggested response, transcript, and speech report in `src/components/session-report.tsx:21-129`.
- Local profile/history: reports save to browser local storage via `saveSession` in `src/lib/profile.ts:86-95`; profile dashboard lists saved sessions and supports open/delete/clear in `src/components/profile-dashboard.tsx:14-93`.
- Error handling/service readiness: `/api/status` reports missing Gemini/Gradium keys in `src/app/api/status/route.ts:3-6`; UI shows setup notices in `src/components/coach.tsx:404-415`; shared server guard enforces same-origin/rate limit/request limits in `src/lib/server/http.ts:13-84`.

Leave these unchecked or mark as still not demo-ready:

- Clean repo/test state: working tree has unmerged `UU` entries including `README.md`, `.env.example`, `src/components/coach.tsx`, `src/lib/contracts.ts`, `src/lib/server/gemini.ts`, `src/lib/server/gradium.ts`, `src/lib/server/routes.test.ts`, and `src/lib/server/validation.ts`. No conflict markers were found in my targeted source reads, but Git still sees unresolved merge entries.
- Profile tests are ahead of current implementation or from an older contract: `src/lib/profile.test.ts:2` imports `writeProfile`, `upsertSession`, `togglePlanItem`, `summarizeProfile`, and `ProfileSession`, but `src/lib/profile.ts` currently exports `readProfile`, `saveSession`, `deleteSession`, `clearProfile`, `getComparableSessions`, and `compareSession`. The same test expects `readProfile()` to return an array at `src/lib/profile.test.ts:20-25`, while current `readProfile` returns `{ version, sessions }` at `src/lib/profile.ts:64-76`.
- Public live voice deployment: `/api/voice-token` is intentionally localhost-only because there are no accounts/auth; see `requireLocalHost` in `src/app/api/voice-token/route.ts:12-19`. Good for local demo, unchecked for public hosted duplex voice.
- Feedback reliability/full rehearsal acceptance: the path exists, but your current three-turn feedback E2E failure means I would not check “full demo rehearsal passes” or “feedback acceptance complete” yet. The backend also strictly rejects invalid Gemini feedback evidence and returns 502 at `src/lib/server/gemini.ts:81-108`, so model-output compliance is a real demo risk.
- Reports/profile integration should be marked “implemented but unstable” rather than fully done until the failing profile/report tests are reconciled with the current `SavedSession` schema in `src/lib/profile.ts:11-22`.

For the Notion page, I’d check off the feature-build boxes for scenarios, avatar/sunflower, typed chat, manual voice, live voice, reports, local profile, and error notices. I’d leave unchecked: clean test suite, public duplex deployment, final useful-feedback acceptance, and end-to-end demo rehearsal.
