{"id":"3f5d67cd0a05805b8023c53570998144","title":"Hackathon Page","text":"Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3f5d67cd0a05805b8023c53570998144 as of 2026-10-10T15:10:29.739Z: {"title":"Hackathon Page"} null Ideas; Recruitment agent, use voice chat to build profile, build something that actually matches you to jobs, filter out shit, personal recommendation about how you are feeling, what to do, plans, organise something voice chat, takes in info, asks lots of questions to get information on your profile, finds out what is important to you and builds on that, creates dashbaord for you track habits, plans, jobs, etc --- # AI Conversation Coach — Four-Hour Hackathon Build Plan **Date:** 10 October 2026 **Concept:** An AI role-play simulator for conversations people find difficult. The user speaks out loud to a cartoon/metaverse-style character that answers naturally, challenges them, and gives specific feedback at the end. ## Product pitch **Practice the conversations that matter — before having them for real.** Examples: - Job interview with a realistic hiring manager - Asking a boss for a raise - Breaking up / navigating a difficult relationship conversation - Giving or receiving difficult workplace feedback - Negotiating, setting boundaries, apologising, or handling conflict - Custom user-provided scenario The differentiator is **interactive rehearsal and useful feedback**, not photorealistic avatar technology. ## Implementation status — 10 October 2026 Checked items below mean implemented in the current local code, not fully approved for a live demo. The core voice loop, animated sunflower, scenario selection and feedback UI are present. Current tests expose profile/report contract mismatches and browser regressions; final demo acceptance remains open. ### Still to finish / verify - [ ] Reconcile profile/report implementation with its tests, resolve typecheck errors, and verify report saving for all scenarios. - [ ] Resolve the browser-test failures: align changed UI labels and report fixtures, and verify live transcript updates and interruption during playback. - [ ] Complete the Git merge: the index still contains unmerged entries, although inspected source files have no conflict markers. - [ ] Rehearse the complete two-minute Ask for a Raise demo with a real microphone, three turns, spoken replies and useful final feedback; check echo, latency and restart. - [ ] If demonstrating on a public URL, implement protected voice-token issuance. Continuous voice currently permits [localhost](http://localhost) only; final recorded WAV transcription is a separate path. **Fresh audit results:** unit/API tests: 178 passed, 17 failed; browser tests: 21 passed, 6 failed; typecheck failed on profile test/API mismatches. Several browser failures use outdated labels or incompatible report fixtures; they do not by themselves prove the corresponding feature is absent. The three-turn browser test reached and displayed feedback before failing on its old restart-button label. **Verification basis:** current source and fresh automated checks; provider calls in these tests are mocked. Existing README live-provider checks are historical evidence, not a fresh physical-microphone rehearsal. Other work was changing the checkout during this audit, so this is a point-in-time snapshot. ## Scope: what we actually ship in four hours **Must have** - [x] Choose a scenario and difficulty (friendly / neutral / challenging) - [x] Display one premade cartoon avatar - [x] User speaks with live chat - [x] Gradium transcribes the user's speech - [x] Gemini generates a brief in-character response using conversation history - [x] Gradium turns the response into speech - [x] Avatar switches among idle, listening and speaking animations - [x] End Session generates a short feedback report **Originally cut / optional scope** Unchecked exclusions below are intentional scope cuts, not remaining MVP requirements. Continuous voice and reporting were subsequently added as noted. - [ ] Custom avatar creation from a photo - [ ] Photorealistic lip-sync, body tracking or elaborate gestures - [ ] Authentication, payment, database or saved accounts - [x] Full-duplex voice interruptions and overlapping speech — subsequently implemented as local continuous voice with interruption handling; playback-interruption regression still needs verification. - [ ] Complex environments, multi-character scenes, multiplayer - [ ] Sophisticated analytics and long transcripts dashboard — partially exceeded: local profiles, saved transcripts, score trends, answer reviews and speech metrics exist; profile/report integration checks are still failing. Photo-to-avatar is not required for this MVP. A premade stylized character plus basic lip movement is sufficient for the demo. ## Proposed technology stack
Layer Technology Responsibility
UI Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind Scenario picker, voice screen, results
Conversation brain Gemini Flash via @google/genai Role-play, follow-up questions, feedback
Voice recognition Gradium STT Convert user's mic audio to text
Voice generation Gradium TTS Read Gemini's answer in character
Avatar Animated 2D SVG **or** premade GLB/VRM Show idle/listening/speaking states
API orchestration Next.js route handlers Protect API keys; coordinate services
Media Browser microphone, HTMLAudioElement Capture/play voice audio
**Choice:** For a reliable four-hour build, prefer a polished animated 2D portrait. Use a premade 3D GLB/VRM only if it already loads and animates. Building an avatar engine is not the product. **Avoid Gemini Live for this particular prototype:** If Gradium must supply both STT and TTS, use Gemini for **text conversation**. Gemini Live's own native audio capabilities would duplicate part of the Gradium pipeline. ## End-to-end architecture 1. User selects scenario + difficulty. 2. Browser records one answer using push-to-talk. 3. POST recorded audio to server API route. 4. Backend sends supported audio to Gradium speech-to-text; obtains a transcript. 5. Backend sends transcript and previous conversation turns to Gemini. 6. Gemini replies as the chosen character, usually 1–3 spoken sentences; backend appends that turn to history. 7. Backend sends Gemini's reply to Gradium text-to-speech and receives audio. 8. Frontend plays the audio and switches avatar to **speaking**. 9. Playback ends; avatar returns to **idle/listening**. 10. User can repeat until they press **End Session**. 11. Gemini evaluates the transcript against a rubric and returns 2 strengths, 2 improvements and 1 suggested better response. **Conceptual flow:** User microphone → Gradium STT → Gemini Flash + history → Gradium TTS → spoken audio + animated avatar. ## Quick setup 1. Get a [Gemini API key](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey). 2. Get a [Gradium API key](https://studio.gradium.ai/). 3. Scaffold a Next.js project and install the Google GenAI SDK. 4. Keep keys on the backend. Never expose Gradium/Gemini keys through NEXT_PUBLIC environment variables. ```bash npx create-next-app@latest conversation-coach cd conversation-coach npm install @google/genai ``` Create .env.local: ```bash GEMINI_API_KEY=your_key GRADIUM_API_KEY=your_key ``` Suggested routes: - POST /api/transcribe — receive user audio; Gradium STT; return text - POST /api/converse — scenario + difficulty + conversation history + user message; Gemini; return reply - POST /api/speak — text; Gradium TTS; return playable WAV audio - POST /api/feedback — conversation transcript + scenario; Gemini; return structured feedback ## Gemini implementation example ```typescript import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"; const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY, }); const response = await ai.models.generateContent({ model: "gemini-2.5-flash", contents: "I'd like to discuss a salary increase.", config: { systemInstruction: "You are a skeptical but fair manager. The user is practising asking for a raise. " + "Stay in character. Ask challenging but believable follow-up questions. " + "Respond in 1–3 natural spoken sentences. Do not coach until the session ends.", }, }); console.log(response.text); ``` For real conversations, send a chat session/history containing **all prior turns**, not only the latest utterance. Keep the role-play consistent with scenario, role and difficulty. Keep replies short to lower latency. ## Gradium voice integration API base: [https://api.gradium.ai](https://api.gradium.ai) - **Speech-to-text:** POST /api/post/speech/asr - **Text-to-speech:** POST /api/post/speech/tts - Follow current official REST request/response details; validate with one sample before building the whole UI. Example server-side TTS request: ```typescript const response = await fetch( "https://api.gradium.ai/api/post/speech/tts", { method: "POST", headers: { "x-api-key": process.env.GRADIUM_API_KEY!, "Content-Type": "application/json", }, body: JSON.stringify({ text: "Why do you believe you deserve a raise?", voice_id: "YTpq7expH9539ERJ", output_format: "wav", only_audio: true, }), } ); if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Gradium TTS failed"); const audio = await response.arrayBuffer(); ``` Return the WAV from the server to the browser with the correct audio content type. Choose an available voice ID from the Gradium docs/dashboard if the example changes. **Important STT gotcha:** MediaRecorder may output WebM/Opus in the browser. Do **not** label WebM as WAV. Either record/encode PCM WAV or convert correctly server-side. Parse the STT response according to the current Gradium docs (including NDJSON segments if returned), concatenating relevant recognised text. **Latency choice:** push-to-talk instead of continuous full-duplex streaming. Finish one turn, get text, generate response, synthesize and play audio, then resume listening. ## Cartoon avatar implementation **Fastest:** animated SVG / 2D character with subtle bobbing, periodic blink and a two-state mouth. Use CSS or Framer Motion if already installed. **If 3D is essential:** use one licensed premade GLB/VRM avatar + Three.js / React Three Fiber; a compatible VRM can use three-vrm for expressions. Frame the upper torso. Avoid the avatar editor entirely. Ready Player Me's former public offering should not be assumed available. Animation states: - **idle**: breathing/bobbing, occasional blink - **listening**: face forward, slight attentiveness - **speaking**: mouth toggles, small nod/head sway during TTS playback ```typescript audio.onplay = () => setIsSpeaking(true); audio.onended = () => setIsSpeaking(false); audio.onerror = () => setIsSpeaking(false); ``` This is an intentionally approximate speaking animation, not phoneme-accurate lip-sync. If there is no mouth blendshape, use an SVG mouth or simple mesh swap instead. ## Scenarios and persona instructions ### Job interview "You are an experienced interviewer assessing a candidate. Ask one question at a time. Demand specific examples and probe vague claims. Remain professional. Do not reveal a rubric or provide coaching until the session ends." ### Asking for a raise "You are the user's manager. You are skeptical but fair about salary increases. Ask for evidence of performance, impact and market value. Raise natural objections. Keep replies concise and conversational." ### Breakup or emotionally difficult conversation "You are the other party in a difficult but respectful relationship conversation. React in a believable, emotionally nuanced way while avoiding threats, manipulation or abuse. Let the user practise empathy and boundaries." ### Difficult feedback "You are a coworker receiving uncomfortable feedback. Start a little defensive, but become more receptive to clear, respectful and specific communication." ### Difficulty settings - **Friendly:** collaborative, gentle objections, lower pressure - **Neutral:** realistic responses and a few challenges - **Challenging:** probing objections, skepticism, follow-up questions without unnecessary hostility System instruction for every scenario: **Stay in character during practice; ask one question at a time; speak naturally in 1–3 sentences; do not prematurely deliver feedback.** A separate Gemini request should generate the final report. ## Interface / demo flow 1. **Landing:** "Practice difficult conversations with AI" 2. **Scenario cards:** Interview / Salary raise / Relationship / Difficult feedback / Custom 3. **Difficulty:** Friendly / Neutral / Challenging 4. **Conversation:** central cartoon avatar, animated state, push-to-talk mic button, small transcript, End Session 5. **Results:** two strengths, two improvements, recommended alternative phrasing; optionally restart at a harder difficulty Demo storyline: select **Ask for a Raise** → speak a salary request → manager challenges the justification by voice → respond once more → End Session → concise actionable report. ## Four-hour sprint checklist ### 00:00–00:45 — Gemini + skeleton UI - [x] Scaffold Next.js; create scenario picker - [x] Add /api/converse and persona prompts - [x] Verify a typed message gets an in-character Gemini response **Checkpoint:** text role-play works, even without voice. ### 00:45–01:40 — Gradium TTS - [x] Create /api/speak - [x] Turn a fixed sentence into playable speech - [x] Wire Gemini responses to automatic audio playback **Checkpoint:** click a button; character's response is heard. ### 01:40–02:35 — Microphone + STT - [x] Record short user turn - [x] Convert to compatible audio encoding - [x] Create /api/transcribe, parse recognized text - [x] Chain transcription → Gemini → TTS **Checkpoint:** complete two-way voice interaction works. ### 02:35–03:20 — Avatar animation - [x] Render one premade 2D or 3D avatar - [x] Implement idle/listening/speaking states - [x] Hook speaking state to TTS audio playback **Checkpoint:** avatar visibly responds when AI speaks. ### 03:20–04:00 — Feedback + reliability + demo - [x] Add the scenario/difficulty presets - [x] End Session report (2 strengths, 2 improvements, improved phrasing) - [x] Handle microphone denied, empty audio and failed API requests - [ ] Rehearse a complete 2-minute walkthrough **Checkpoint:** demo works from start to finish. ## What could go wrong / fallback plan - **STT audio incompatibility:** test encoding immediately; if blocked, temporarily allow typed input so the rest of the demo remains usable. - **3D avatar takes too long:** revert to a clean 2D SVG character. Animation quality is secondary. - **TTS latency:** keep Gemini replies short, use a loading/speaking state, and avoid huge transcripts per request. - **API quota or model problems:** test keys at the start, show recoverable errors, and have a prerecorded walkthrough/video only as backup for the presentation. - **Unsafe/awkward role-play:** give scenarios clear guardrails; keep relationship simulations respectful and clearly fictional. - **Privacy:** avoid storing raw recordings in MVP unless necessary; get consent if recording or keeping a transcript. ## Definition of done - [x] A user can select **Ask for a Raise** - [x] Their spoken words are recognized by Gradium - [x] Gemini responds in character based on conversation history - [x] Gradium delivers the response in a spoken voice - [x] A cartoon avatar animates when speaking - [x] User can complete at least three turns - [ ] End Session produces clear, useful feedback - [ ] One complete demo can run without editing source code or manually calling APIs ## Copy-paste prompt for Cursor / coding agent > Build a hackathon MVP called Conversation Coach using Next.js App Router, TypeScript and Tailwind. Users select an interview, salary negotiation, breakup conversation, or difficult feedback scenario. Gemini is the conversation AI, using @google/genai with gemini-2.5-flash and full multi-turn history. Gradium must handle both speech-to-text and text-to-speech using the documented REST endpoints. Implement server-side routes /api/transcribe, /api/converse, /api/speak, and /api/feedback; keep keys in GEMINI_API_KEY and GRADIUM_API_KEY server environment variables. Use browser push-to-talk recording, and ensure WAV compatibility for Gradium STT (do not send WebM marked as WAV). Parse Gradium STT responses correctly. Use Gradium TTS with WAV audio output and play it with an HTMLAudioElement. Build a playful, clean cartoon avatar UI with idle/listening/speaking states and simple mouth motion during playback. Prioritize a functional voice loop over complex 3D. Include friendly, neutral and challenging difficulty settings; keep Gemini in character with short spoken replies. Maintain conversation history. Add End Session feedback with 2 strengths, 2 improvements and a suggested better response from Gemini. Add loading, microphone and API error states. No database, authentication, payments, photo-to-avatar generation or unnecessary dependencies. Implement incrementally: text conversation first, then TTS, then STT, then avatar, then feedback. ## Documentation / links - [Gemini API keys](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) - [Google GenAI / Gemini API](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content) - [Gradium Studio](https://studio.gradium.ai/) - [Gradium speech-to-text REST guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/speech-to-text-rest) - [Gradium text-to-speech REST guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/text-to-speech-rest) - [three-vrm for optional 3D avatar](https://github.com/pixiv/three-vrm) **Execution rule:** Do not spend the first two hours making the avatar pretty. First prove the voice conversation loop. The avatar is a presentation layer, not the core value. Animation quality is secondary. - **TTS latency:** keep Gemini replies short, use a loading/speaking state, and avoid huge transcripts per request. - **API quota or model problems:** test keys at the start, show recoverable errors, and have a prerecorded walkthrough/video only as backup for the presentation. - **Unsafe/awkward role-play:** give scenarios clear guardrails; keep relationship simulations respectful and clearly fictional. - **Privacy:** avoid storing raw recordings in MVP unless necessary; get consent if recording or keeping a transcript. ## Definition of done - [x] A user can select **Ask for a Raise** - [x] Their spoken words are recognized by Gradium - [x] Gemini responds in character based on conversation history - [x] Gradium delivers the response in a spoken voice - [x] A cartoon avatar animates when speaking - [x] User can complete at least three turns - [ ] End Session produces clear, useful feedback - [ ] One complete demo can run without editing source code or manually calling APIs ## Copy-paste prompt for Cursor / coding agent > Build a hackathon MVP called Conversation Coach using Next.js App Router, TypeScript and Tailwind. Users select an interview, salary negotiation, breakup conversation, or difficult feedback scenario. Gemini is the conversation AI, using @google/genai with gemini-2.5-flash and full multi-turn history. Gradium must handle both speech-to-text and text-to-speech using the documented REST endpoints. Implement server-side routes /api/transcribe, /api/converse, /api/speak, and /api/feedback; keep keys in GEMINI_API_KEY and GRADIUM_API_KEY server environment variables. Use browser push-to-talk recording, and ensure WAV compatibility for Gradium STT (do not send WebM marked as WAV). Parse Gradium STT responses correctly. Use Gradium TTS with WAV audio output and play it with an HTMLAudioElement. Build a playful, clean cartoon avatar UI with idle/listening/speaking states and simple mouth motion during playback. Prioritize a functional voice loop over complex 3D. Include friendly, neutral and challenging difficulty settings; keep Gemini in character with short spoken replies. Maintain conversation history. Add End Session feedback with 2 strengths, 2 improvements and a suggested better response from Gemini. Add loading, microphone and API error states. No database, authentication, payments, photo-to-avatar generation or unnecessary dependencies. Implement incrementally: text conversation first, then TTS, then STT, then avatar, then feedback. ## Documentation / links - [Gemini API keys](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) - [Google GenAI / Gemini API](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content) - [Gradium Studio](https://studio.gradium.ai/) - [Gradium speech-to-text REST guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/speech-to-text-rest) - [Gradium text-to-speech REST guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/text-to-speech-rest) - [three-vrm for optional 3D avatar](https://github.com/pixiv/three-vrm) **Execution rule:** Do not spend the first two hours making the avatar pretty. First prove the voice conversation loop. The avatar is a presentation layer, not the core value. Features For Demo
